decisions.title: Discovery is derived from and bound to one exact issuer
decisions.specification: OpenID Connect Discovery 1.0 incorporating errata set 2
decisions.section: OpenID Connect Discovery 1.0 [Sections 4 and 4.3](https://openid.net/specs/openid-connect-discovery-1_0.html#ProviderConfig) and OpenID Connect Core 1.0 [Section 3.1.3.7](https://openid.net/specs/openid-connect-core-1_0.html#IDTokenValidation)
decisions.issue: Discovery defines an append rule for issuers with paths, while URL normalization and upstream verifier compatibility can otherwise treat case, ports, paths, or trailing slashes as aliases.
interpretations: Normalize equivalent URLs; accept provider aliases; use a caller-supplied discovery URL; or derive the well-known URL from one configured issuer and require exact returned and token issuer strings.
decisions.peer_behavior: Providers expose the standard well-known document, but libraries and deployments differ in URL normalization and issuer-alias tolerance.
decisions.selected_behavior: Derive `/.well-known/openid-configuration` using the Discovery append rule. Reject configured issuer query, fragment, userinfo, unsupported schemes, and non-loopback HTTP. The configured issuer, metadata `issuer`, and token `iss` must match byte for byte.
decisions.rationale: The cited authority leaves this boundary ambiguous or incomplete, so the selected fail-closed behavior is documented as package hardening rather than a specification requirement.
decisions.security_consequences: Exact binding prevents cross-tenant metadata and token substitution. Discovery performs one bounded initialization request rather than following caller- or token-selected locations.
decisions.resource_consequences: Exact binding prevents cross-tenant metadata and token substitution. Discovery performs one bounded initialization request rather than following caller- or token-selected locations.
decisions.compatibility_consequences: Standard exact issuers, including path issuers, interoperate. Alias, normalization, and trailing-slash differences accepted by permissive peers are intentionally rejected.
decisions.wire_consequences: Standard exact issuers, including path issuers, interoperate. Alias, normalization, and trailing-slash differences accepted by permissive peers are intentionally rejected.
decisions.upstream_status: Discovery errata set 2 defines the issuer append and exact-match requirements; no alias registry is defined.
decisions.reconsider_when: A future OpenID profile standardizes issuer aliases with downgrade-resistant discovery and token-binding semantics.

decisions.title: Provider metadata is strict, bounded, and capability-complete
decisions.specification: OpenID Connect Discovery 1.0 incorporating errata set 2
decisions.section: OpenID Connect Discovery 1.0 [Section 3](https://openid.net/specs/openid-connect-discovery-1_0.html#ProviderMetadata) and RFC 8259 [Sections 4 and 8.2](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8259.html#section-4)
decisions.issue: Discovery defines required and optional members but does not settle duplicate JSON names, explicit null for optional members, Unicode whitespace in string lists, or implementation resource ceilings.
interpretations: Ignore malformed optional members; accept last duplicate; coerce null to absent; split on all Unicode whitespace; or reject ambiguous standard metadata before key retrieval.
decisions.peer_behavior: Real Google, Keycloak, and Dex profiles use conventional unique JSON. General decoders commonly accept duplicate names and null values more permissively.
decisions.selected_behavior: Require one bounded JSON object and an exact JSON response media type. Standard members must be unique and correctly typed; explicit null is not absence. Response types use one ASCII-space separator, supported subject types are unique, advertised scopes include `openid`, and signing algorithms include RS256 plus every configured algorithm.
decisions.rationale: The cited authority leaves this boundary ambiguous or incomplete, so the selected fail-closed behavior is documented as package hardening rather than a specification requirement.
decisions.security_consequences: Strict metadata prevents parser differentials and capability downgrade. Header, body, object, member, collection, key, and initialization bounds apply before retaining provider data.
decisions.resource_consequences: Strict metadata prevents parser differentials and capability downgrade. Header, body, object, member, collection, key, and initialization bounds apply before retaining provider data.
decisions.compatibility_consequences: Standards-compliant provider metadata remains unchanged. Malformed-but-tolerated metadata fails construction instead of being silently normalized.
decisions.wire_consequences: Standards-compliant provider metadata remains unchanged. Malformed-but-tolerated metadata fails construction instead of being silently normalized.
decisions.upstream_status: The OpenID Foundation conformance profiles informed the matrix; they do not replace package-level hostile JSON and allocation policy.
decisions.reconsider_when: Discovery publishes a new metadata member or erratum requiring a different null, list, or algorithm-advertisement interpretation.

decisions.title: Provider-directed endpoints are HTTPS but may be cross-origin
decisions.specification: OpenID Connect Discovery 1.0 incorporating errata set 2
decisions.section: OpenID Connect Discovery 1.0 [Sections 3 and 4.3](https://openid.net/specs/openid-connect-discovery-1_0.html#ProviderConfigurationResponse) and RFC 9110 [Section 15.4](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9110.html#section-15.4)
decisions.issue: Discovery permits metadata to direct clients to endpoints, including a JWKS origin different from the issuer, but does not define deployment-specific DNS, IP, port, proxy, or redirect trust.
interpretations: Require same origin; follow ordinary redirects; permit arbitrary HTTP; embed a global private-network ban; or allow valid HTTPS metadata while delegating topology policy to an injected transport.
decisions.peer_behavior: Google's issuer and JWKS use different HTTPS origins. Default Go HTTP clients follow redirects unless explicitly hardened.
decisions.selected_behavior: Accept valid HTTPS provider endpoints, including cross-origin JWKS. Reject redirects, userinfo, fragments, unsupported schemes, and non-loopback HTTP. `InsecureHTTP` permits loopback development only. Deployments needing DNS, address, port, proxy, or origin restrictions must supply a hardened `HTTPClient` transport.
decisions.rationale: The cited authority leaves this boundary ambiguous or incomplete, so the selected fail-closed behavior is documented as package hardening rather than a specification requirement.
decisions.security_consequences: Redirect denial prevents authority changes after validation. Provider-directed egress remains an explicit trust consequence, while caller transport policy can enforce deployment topology without breaking legitimate private or cross-origin issuers.
decisions.resource_consequences: Redirect denial prevents authority changes after validation. Provider-directed egress remains an explicit trust consequence, while caller transport policy can enforce deployment topology without breaking legitimate private or cross-origin issuers.
decisions.compatibility_consequences: Google-style cross-origin JWKS works. Redirecting and non-loopback plaintext providers are intentionally incompatible; custom transport restrictions may further narrow deployment compatibility.
decisions.wire_consequences: Google-style cross-origin JWKS works. Redirecting and non-loopback plaintext providers are intentionally incompatible; custom transport restrictions may further narrow deployment compatibility.
decisions.upstream_status: Discovery permits endpoint URLs but does not provide a universal SSRF policy; that deployment boundary remains caller-owned and documented.
decisions.reconsider_when: Discovery or a deployment profile defines enforceable endpoint-origin constraints compatible with supported providers.

decisions.title: Algorithms and public JWK candidates must agree exactly
decisions.specification: RFC 7518 JSON Web Algorithms
decisions.section: OpenID Connect Core 1.0 [Sections 2 and 3.1.3.7](https://openid.net/specs/openid-connect-core-1_0.html#IDToken), OpenID Connect Discovery 1.0 [`id_token_signing_alg_values_supported`](https://openid.net/specs/openid-connect-discovery-1_0.html#ProviderMetadata), RFC 7517 [Sections 4 and 5](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc7517.html#section-4), and RFC 7518 [Section 3](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc7518.html#section-3)
decisions.issue: Provider metadata, token `alg`, JWK metadata, key shape, and `kid` can disagree; sets can also contain unrelated encryption keys or ambiguous signing candidates.
interpretations: Try every key; infer algorithms from keys; accept HMAC client-secret signatures; reject all unrelated keys; or filter valid public signing candidates and require unambiguous exact agreement.
decisions.peer_behavior: General OIDC libraries support configurable algorithms and key sets, with differing treatment of missing IDs and unrelated keys.
decisions.selected_behavior: Support configured asymmetric RS, PS, ES, and EdDSA families only when advertised by the provider. Candidate keys must be public, algorithm- and shape-compatible, and signing-capable; encryption-only keys are ignored. Ambiguous permitted candidates require `kid`. RSA is 2048 through 8192 bits and EC/EdDSA shape must match exactly.
decisions.rationale: The cited authority leaves this boundary ambiguous or incomplete, so the selected fail-closed behavior is documented as package hardening rather than a specification requirement.
decisions.security_consequences: Explicit agreement prevents HMAC/asymmetric confusion and key trial amplification. Key count and RSA upper bounds limit verification work.
decisions.resource_consequences: Explicit agreement prevents HMAC/asymmetric confusion and key trial amplification. Key count and RSA upper bounds limit verification work.
decisions.compatibility_consequences: Supported provider-issued asymmetric tokens interoperate. Symmetric, encrypted, weak, private, ambiguous, or unadvertised tokens and keys are rejected by policy.
decisions.wire_consequences: Supported provider-issued asymmetric tokens interoperate. Symmetric, encrypted, weak, private, ambiguous, or unadvertised tokens and keys are rejected by policy.
decisions.upstream_status: Discovery requires RS256 support and advertises additional algorithms; configuration does not silently inherit the provider's entire algorithm set.
decisions.reconsider_when: A concrete profile requires encrypted or symmetric ID tokens and can provide separate bounded key and client-secret handling.

decisions.title: Compact token JSON is inspected before upstream verification
decisions.specification: RFC 7515 JSON Web Signature
decisions.section: OpenID Connect Core 1.0 [Section 2](https://openid.net/specs/openid-connect-core-1_0.html#IDToken), RFC 7515 [Sections 3.1 and 5.2](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc7515.html#section-3.1), RFC 8259 [Sections 4, 6, and 8.2](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8259.html#section-4)
decisions.issue: Upstream parsers can accept duplicate members, malformed Unicode replacement, excessive nesting, padded encodings, or lossy numeric decoding differently.
interpretations: Delegate all parsing; keep first or last duplicate; coerce numbers through float64; support JSON JOSE serialization; or enforce one strict bounded compact representation first.
decisions.peer_behavior: Core providers issue compact signed ID tokens, while generic JSON and JOSE parser edge behavior differs.
decisions.selected_behavior: Require three non-empty strict unpadded base64url segments within `MaxTokenBytes`. Protected header and claims are bounded unique-member JSON objects with valid Unicode and correctly typed standard members. Claims are decoded losslessly without float64 coercion. Unsupported distributed-claim protocol fields are rejected.
decisions.rationale: The cited authority leaves this boundary ambiguous or incomplete, so the selected fail-closed behavior is documented as package hardening rather than a specification requirement.
decisions.security_consequences: Parser differential, duplicate-key smuggling, number precision loss, nested allocation, and malformed Unicode fail before trust or principal construction.
decisions.resource_consequences: Parser differential, duplicate-key smuggling, number precision loss, nested allocation, and malformed Unicode fail before trust or principal construction.
decisions.compatibility_consequences: Conventional compact provider tokens remain compatible. Permissive or non-compact encodings are rejected rather than normalized. Private JSON numbers preserve exact lexical value in the principal.
decisions.wire_consequences: Conventional compact provider tokens remain compatible. Permissive or non-compact encodings are rejected rather than normalized. Private JSON numbers preserve exact lexical value in the principal.
decisions.upstream_status: No erratum mandates permissive duplicate or lossy-number behavior; strict parsing is package-owned hardening.
decisions.reconsider_when: Core adopts another mandatory ID-token serialization with equivalent deterministic and bounded parsing rules.

decisions.title: Audience, authorized party, and subject form one principal boundary
decisions.specification: OpenID Connect Core 1.0 incorporating errata set 2
decisions.issue: Core permits multiple audiences and optional `azp` in some cases, while applications need to prevent trusted-client tokens from carrying arbitrary additional recipients or malformed subjects.
interpretations: Check only that client ID appears; accept any extra audience; ignore `azp`; normalize subject text; or require an explicit complete recipient and subject policy.
decisions.peer_behavior: OIDC libraries commonly check client membership but may not reject additional audiences unless callers add policy.
decisions.selected_behavior: Require client ID in a unique audience set. Every extra audience must be explicitly trusted. `azp`, when present, equals client ID and is mandatory for multiple audiences. Subject is non-empty ASCII and at most 255 bytes. Exact issuer and subject become the principal identity.
decisions.rationale: The cited authority leaves this boundary ambiguous or incomplete, so the selected fail-closed behavior is documented as package hardening rather than a specification requirement.
decisions.security_consequences: Prevents cross-client token reuse and ambiguous principal identifiers. Audience and subject sizes remain bounded before principal allocation.
decisions.resource_consequences: Prevents cross-client token reuse and ambiguous principal identifiers. Audience and subject sizes remain bounded before principal allocation.
decisions.compatibility_consequences: Single-client and explicitly trusted multi-audience tokens work. Tokens with duplicate or untrusted audiences, wrong or missing required `azp`, Unicode subjects, or oversized subjects are rejected.
decisions.wire_consequences: Single-client and explicitly trusted multi-audience tokens work. Tokens with duplicate or untrusted audiences, wrong or missing required `azp`, Unicode subjects, or oversized subjects are rejected.
decisions.upstream_status: Core defines audience and `azp`; rejection of unlisted additional audiences and the subject byte profile are explicit application hardening.
decisions.reconsider_when: A deployment needs another subject syntax or audience delegation model with an explicit non-ambiguous principal mapping.

decisions.title: NumericDate validation preserves fractions and one skew policy
decisions.specification: RFC 7519 JSON Web Token
decisions.section: OpenID Connect Core 1.0 [Sections 2 and 3.1.3.7](https://openid.net/specs/openid-connect-core-1_0.html#IDTokenValidation) and RFC 7519 [`NumericDate`](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc7519.html#section-2)
decisions.issue: NumericDate permits non-integer values, libraries can truncate fractions, and Core permits implementation-specific clock skew without defining every equality edge.
interpretations: Truncate to seconds; use wall clock repeatedly; ignore `iat`; configure independent leeway; or preserve exact fractions against one injected clock and symmetric skew.
decisions.peer_behavior: OIDC and JWT libraries differ in fractional parsing and optional claim checks.
decisions.selected_behavior: Require `iat` and `exp`; validate optional `nbf` and `auth_time`; preserve fractional seconds; read the configured clock deterministically; and apply one bounded non-negative `ClockSkew` to every temporal boundary. Epoch `auth_time` is valid.
decisions.rationale: The cited authority leaves this boundary ambiguous or incomplete, so the selected fail-closed behavior is documented as package hardening rather than a specification requirement.
decisions.security_consequences: Exact comparisons avoid truncation acceptance windows. Explicit skew bounds replay tolerance and makes tests deterministic.
decisions.resource_consequences: Exact comparisons avoid truncation acceptance windows. Explicit skew bounds replay tolerance and makes tests deterministic.
decisions.compatibility_consequences: Integer and fractional NumericDate values interoperate. Tokens accepted only because a peer truncates fractions or ignores a temporal claim are deliberately rejected.
decisions.wire_consequences: Integer and fractional NumericDate values interoperate. Tokens accepted only because a peer truncates fractions or ignores a temporal claim are deliberately rejected.
decisions.upstream_status: Core permits reasonable skew but does not define its amount; the package's default and upper bound are explicit implementation policy.
decisions.reconsider_when: A profile mandates per-claim leeway or higher-precision time semantics.

decisions.title: Nonce replay ownership stays with one caller callback
decisions.specification: OpenID Connect Core 1.0 incorporating errata set 2
decisions.issue: Core requires nonce comparison when sent but cannot define application storage, atomic consumption, expiry, replay coordination, or callback failure handling.
interpretations: Store nonce in the package; compare a caller string; make checking optional even when configured; invoke before other validation; or delegate atomic single-use consumption after all other checks.
decisions.peer_behavior: OIDC libraries commonly return nonce for callers to compare. Replay stores remain application-specific.
decisions.selected_behavior: `NonceValidator` owns presence, expiry, equality, and atomic single-use consumption. Invoke it once only after signature, binding, and every other claim succeeds. Contain callback panic and redact callback errors as rejection; preserve callback context cancellation as authentication unavailability.
decisions.rationale: The cited authority leaves this application boundary optional or undefined, so the package records a stable caller-facing policy without presenting it as specification-mandated.
decisions.security_consequences: Invalid tokens cannot consume valid nonce state, and concurrent replay races are resolved by the caller's atomic store. The package retains no nonce or replay database.
decisions.resource_consequences: Invalid tokens cannot consume valid nonce state, and concurrent replay races are resolved by the caller's atomic store. The package retains no nonce or replay database.
decisions.compatibility_consequences: Token bytes are unchanged. Applications enabling nonce validation must provide a concurrency-safe consuming callback; omission leaves nonce policy caller-owned.
decisions.wire_consequences: Token bytes are unchanged. Applications enabling nonce validation must provide a concurrency-safe consuming callback; omission leaves nonce policy caller-owned.
decisions.upstream_status: Core owns nonce semantics; storage and atomic replay prevention are deliberately outside the protocol package.
decisions.reconsider_when: A reusable nonce-store adapter can be added without embedding persistence or weakening caller lifecycle ownership.

decisions.title: Front-channel token hashes are validated only from explicit call inputs
decisions.specification: OpenID Connect Core 1.0 incorporating errata set 2
decisions.section: OpenID Connect Core 1.0 [`at_hash`](https://openid.net/specs/openid-connect-core-1_0.html#CodeIDToken) and [`c_hash`](https://openid.net/specs/openid-connect-core-1_0.html#HybridIDToken2) validation rules
decisions.issue: Whether `at_hash` or `c_hash` is required depends on authorization flow and returned values that cannot be inferred from the ID token alone. EdDSA also names no hash family for OIDC half-hash selection.
interpretations: Ignore both claims; infer the flow; require both universally; accept claims without caller values; or validate each only when its opaque source value is supplied explicitly.
decisions.peer_behavior: OIDC clients often perform these checks in flow-specific code rather than generic bearer validation.
decisions.selected_behavior: `ValidateIDToken` validates `at_hash` for non-empty access-token input and `c_hash` for non-empty authorization-code input using the signing algorithm's 256/384/512 hash family. A requested binding requires the claim and exact value. EdDSA with requested binding is rejected because no hash family is defined. `ValidateBearer` supplies no front-channel values.
decisions.rationale: The cited authority leaves this application boundary optional or undefined, so the package records a stable caller-facing policy without presenting it as specification-mandated.
decisions.security_consequences: Explicit inputs prevent false assurance from an inferred flow and bind returned artifacts against substitution. Hash work is bounded by caller-supplied token/code length and call lifetime.
decisions.resource_consequences: Explicit inputs prevent false assurance from an inferred flow and bind returned artifacts against substitution. Hash work is bounded by caller-supplied token/code length and call lifetime.
decisions.compatibility_consequences: Correct code, implicit, and hybrid responses interoperate when callers provide their returned values. Callers omitting those inputs do not receive a claim of front-channel binding.
decisions.wire_consequences: Correct code, implicit, and hybrid responses interoperate when callers provide their returned values. Callers omitting those inputs do not receive a claim of front-channel binding.
decisions.upstream_status: Core defines flow-specific requirements; this API exposes rather than guesses the missing flow context.
decisions.reconsider_when: A higher-level authorization-flow package can guarantee and supply these values automatically without changing this validator's narrow boundary.

decisions.title: Metadata and JWKS refresh together, expire fail closed, and reject rollback
decisions.specification: RFC 9111 HTTP Caching
decisions.section: OpenID Connect Discovery 1.0 [Section 4.3](https://openid.net/specs/openid-connect-discovery-1_0.html#ProviderConfigurationResponse), RFC 9111 [Sections 4.2 and 5.2](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9111.html#section-4.2), and RFC 7517 [Section 5](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc7517.html#section-5)
decisions.issue: OIDC does not define refresh synchronization, unknown-key probes, stale-key outage behavior, metadata/JWKS atomicity, or rollback after a key is retired.
interpretations: Cache forever; serve stale during outage; refetch on every unknown ID; refresh only keys; accept provider rollback; or maintain one bounded fail-closed state transition.
decisions.peer_behavior: Remote key caches commonly retry unknown IDs and serve cached keys, but cooldown, expiry, metadata changes, and rollback behavior differ.
decisions.selected_behavior: Refresh metadata and JWKS as one synchronized transition. Clamp HTTP freshness to configured bounds and apply per-instance early jitter. After cooldown, an unknown `kid` triggers one shared probe. Known keys work only while fresh; required refresh failure is cached until the minimum interval and fails closed after expiry. Successful removal retires key material for this validator lifetime; later rollback cannot reintroduce it. A changed `jwks_uri` clears validators for the old URL.
decisions.rationale: The cited authority leaves this boundary ambiguous or incomplete, so the selected fail-closed behavior is documented as package hardening rather than a specification requirement.
decisions.security_consequences: Cooldown and synchronization prevent attacker-driven request storms. Fail-closed expiry and bounded retired-key history prevent indefinite stale trust and rollback within one process, at the cost of availability during provider outage.
decisions.resource_consequences: Cooldown and synchronization prevent attacker-driven request storms. Fail-closed expiry and bounded retired-key history prevent indefinite stale trust and rollback within one process, at the cost of availability during provider outage.
decisions.compatibility_consequences: Normal provider rotation works before or at freshness expiry. Reintroducing retired key material or relying on stale keys after expiry is intentionally incompatible. Reconstructing a validator resets process-local retirement history.
decisions.wire_consequences: Normal provider rotation works before or at freshness expiry. Reintroducing retired key material or relying on stale keys after expiry is intentionally incompatible. Reconstructing a validator resets process-local retirement history.
decisions.upstream_status: HTTP controls freshness, but fail-closed expiry and retired-key rollback prevention are explicit package security policy.
decisions.reconsider_when: A provider profile supplies authenticated push invalidation or a shared cache protocol with equivalent bounded rollback protection.

decisions.title: Refresh concurrency is synchronous, bounded, and caller-cancelable
decisions.specification: RFC 9110 HTTP Semantics
decisions.issue: Protocol specifications do not define which caller owns refresh, how waiters cancel, whether refresh starts goroutines, or how one cancellation affects shared state.
interpretations: Spawn background refresh; let every caller fetch; allow unbounded waiters; let owner cancellation poison cooldown; or use one synchronous owner with bounded independent waiters.
decisions.peer_behavior: Cache libraries use background refresh, singleflight, or per-request retrieval with materially different lifecycle behavior.
decisions.selected_behavior: The validator starts no goroutines or timers. One caller synchronously owns each network refresh; admitted waiters are bounded and retain independent contexts. Owner cancellation does not poison another caller's future refresh or shared cooldown. Clock callbacks run outside synchronization. Every response body is closed.
decisions.rationale: The cited authority leaves this boundary ambiguous or incomplete, so the selected fail-closed behavior is documented as package hardening rather than a specification requirement.
decisions.security_consequences: `MaxRefreshWaiters`, request deadlines, body limits, and one owner bound memory, goroutines, sockets, and upstream load. No `Close` method is required because no package-owned background lifetime exists.
decisions.resource_consequences: `MaxRefreshWaiters`, request deadlines, body limits, and one owner bound memory, goroutines, sockets, and upstream load. No `Close` method is required because no package-owned background lifetime exists.
decisions.compatibility_consequences: No OIDC wire change. Validation may return unavailable under waiter saturation or cancellation rather than queue indefinitely. Caller collaborators must honor context and be concurrency-safe.
decisions.wire_consequences: No OIDC wire change. Validation may return unavailable under waiter saturation or cancellation rather than queue indefinitely. Caller collaborators must honor context and be concurrency-safe.
decisions.upstream_status: This is a Go runtime contract layered over protocol messages; no OpenID erratum defines process lifecycle.
decisions.reconsider_when: A background refresh design can prove explicit close ownership, equivalent bounds, and no weaker cancellation or fleet behavior.

decisions.title: Errors are stable, redacted, and preserve only safe cancellation identity
decisions.specification: OpenID Connect Core 1.0 incorporating errata set 2
decisions.section: OpenID Connect Core 1.0 [Section 3.1.3.7](https://openid.net/specs/openid-connect-core-1_0.html#IDTokenValidation) and OpenID Connect Discovery 1.0 [Section 4.4](https://openid.net/specs/openid-connect-discovery-1_0.html#ProviderConfigurationValidation)
decisions.issue: Callers need invalid, rejected, and unavailable distinctions, but provider, callback, token, nonce, key, credential, and response errors can retain secrets or create a validation oracle.
interpretations: Return upstream causes verbatim; expose provider bodies; collapse every error; retain all wrapped causes; or map to stable categories while preserving only context cancellation identity.
decisions.peer_behavior: OIDC libraries expose detailed verifier and HTTP errors useful for tooling but unsafe to return or log directly at an authentication boundary.
decisions.selected_behavior: Empty, wrong-kind, malformed, or oversized credentials are invalid; signature, issuer, claim, nonce, and binding failures are rejected; discovery, JWKS, rollback, timeout, waiter saturation, and cancellation are unavailable. Public errors do not retain arbitrary provider, callback, token, nonce, key, credential, or body text. Safe `context.Canceled` and deadline identity remains detectable.
decisions.rationale: The cited authority leaves this boundary ambiguous or incomplete, so the selected fail-closed behavior is documented as package hardening rather than a specification requirement.
decisions.security_consequences: Redaction prevents secret-bearing errors and low-cardinality categories avoid attacker-controlled telemetry. Operators retain enough classification for retry and availability policy.
decisions.resource_consequences: Redaction prevents secret-bearing errors and low-cardinality categories avoid attacker-controlled telemetry. Operators retain enough classification for retry and availability policy.
decisions.compatibility_consequences: Adapters receive stable authentication categories rather than provider-specific diagnostics. Consumers must use `errors.Is` and `errors.As`, not compare messages or expect raw causes.
decisions.wire_consequences: Adapters receive stable authentication categories rather than provider-specific diagnostics. Consumers must use `errors.Is` and `errors.As`, not compare messages or expect raw causes.
decisions.upstream_status: OpenID defines validation outcomes but not Go error-chain disclosure; this redaction profile is package-owned.
decisions.reconsider_when: A protocol adapter requires a standardized external error code that can map from these categories without retaining sensitive detail.

decisions.title: Provider metadata and ID Tokens use the exact configured issuer
decisions.specification: OpenID Connect Discovery 1.0 incorporating errata set 2
decisions.section: OpenID Connect Discovery 1.0 [Section 4.3](https://openid.net/specs/openid-connect-discovery-1_0.html#ProviderConfigurationValidation) and OpenID Connect Core 1.0 [Section 3.1.3.7](https://openid.net/specs/openid-connect-core-1_0.html#IDTokenValidation)
decisions.issue: Issuer aliases and URL normalization can bind provider metadata or tokens to a different tenant or trust domain than the issuer selected by the client.
interpretations: Normalize equivalent URLs; accept provider aliases; or require byte-for-byte identity between the configured issuer, discovered metadata issuer, and token issuer.
decisions.peer_behavior: Observed providers preserve exact issuer identity, while some libraries accept compatibility aliases or normalized URL forms.
decisions.selected_behavior: The configured issuer, the discovered metadata `issuer`, and the ID Token `iss` claim must match exactly. Alias, case, port, path, and trailing-slash differences are rejected.
decisions.rationale: This preserves Discovery and Core's exact issuer-match requirements separately from URL construction and defensive URL-policy choices.
decisions.security_consequences: Exact identity prevents metadata, key, and token substitution across issuer aliases or tenants.
decisions.resource_consequences: Issuer comparison is bounded by the configured metadata and token limits.
decisions.compatibility_consequences: Providers and clients must use one exact issuer identifier across configuration, discovery, and tokens.
decisions.wire_consequences: A metadata document or ID Token with a non-identical issuer is rejected.
decisions.upstream_status: Discovery Section 4.3 and Core Section 3.1.3.7 require exact issuer identity.
decisions.reconsider_when: A future OpenID profile replaces exact issuer identity with an authenticated alias mechanism.

decisions.title: Discovery metadata contains every required provider member
decisions.specification: OpenID Connect Discovery 1.0 incorporating errata set 2
decisions.issue: A Discovery response without the required provider metadata cannot establish the issuer, authorization endpoint, signing keys, response types, subject types, and ID Token signing algorithms needed by an OpenID client.
interpretations: Infer omitted defaults; accept a partial metadata profile; or reject a response missing any required Discovery member.
decisions.peer_behavior: The pinned Google metadata and representative provider profiles include the required members.
decisions.selected_behavior: Provider metadata must contain non-null, correctly typed `issuer`, `authorization_endpoint`, `jwks_uri`, `response_types_supported`, `subject_types_supported`, and `id_token_signing_alg_values_supported` members.
decisions.rationale: This records Discovery's REQUIRED members without upgrading separately recommended or optional metadata to mandatory status.
decisions.security_consequences: The client never infers a trust endpoint, key location, subject model, or signing capability from missing metadata.
decisions.resource_consequences: Required-member validation runs within the bounded metadata object before JWKS retrieval.
decisions.compatibility_consequences: Partial or null-filled provider metadata is rejected even when a permissive client could infer defaults.
decisions.wire_consequences: A Discovery response missing any required member is invalid.
decisions.upstream_status: Discovery Section 3 marks these six provider metadata members REQUIRED.
decisions.reconsider_when: A later Discovery version changes the required provider metadata set.

decisions.title: Provider authorization and JWKS endpoints use HTTPS
decisions.specification: OpenID Connect Discovery 1.0 incorporating errata set 2
decisions.issue: Provider-directed authorization and key endpoints cross a network trust boundary and Discovery requires them to use HTTPS.
interpretations: Accept any URL scheme; follow provider redirects; or require direct HTTPS endpoints while exposing loopback HTTP only as an explicit non-conformant development extension.
decisions.peer_behavior: The pinned Google and Keycloak provider profiles publish HTTPS endpoints in conformant deployment metadata.
decisions.selected_behavior: Provider `authorization_endpoint` and `jwks_uri` values must use HTTPS. Plain HTTP is rejected except for the explicit loopback-only `InsecureHTTP` development extension, which is outside the conformance claim.
decisions.rationale: This preserves Discovery's HTTPS requirements while clearly excluding the explicit loopback development extension from protocol conformance.
decisions.security_consequences: Production metadata cannot downgrade authorization or signing-key retrieval to unauthenticated transport.
decisions.resource_consequences: URL validation occurs before any network request; redirect and response bounds remain governed separately.
decisions.compatibility_consequences: Production providers must publish direct HTTPS endpoints. Loopback HTTP remains available only through explicit development configuration.
decisions.wire_consequences: Non-HTTPS production endpoint metadata is rejected.
decisions.upstream_status: Discovery Section 3 requires HTTPS for the authorization and JWKS endpoint URLs.
decisions.reconsider_when: A successor Discovery specification defines another authenticated endpoint transport.

decisions.title: ID Token signatures use their declared algorithm and issuer key
decisions.specification: OpenID Connect Core 1.0 incorporating errata set 2
decisions.issue: An ID Token signature must be validated with the algorithm selected for the response and keys belonging to the exact issuer.
interpretations: Trust any library-supported algorithm and compatible key; accept an unadvertised algorithm; or require an advertised configured algorithm and a matching public issuer key.
decisions.peer_behavior: The pinned Keycloak provider issues an RS256 ID Token that validates against its advertised public JWKS.
decisions.selected_behavior: ID Token signatures must validate using the algorithm specified by the protected `alg` header and keys provided by the exact issuer.
decisions.rationale: This preserves Core's mandatory signature validation separately from the package's narrower key-size, key-selection, and supported-algorithm policy.
decisions.security_consequences: Tokens cannot authenticate through an algorithm different from the protected `alg` header or trust material from another issuer.
decisions.resource_consequences: Candidate algorithm and key work remains bounded by configured algorithm and JWKS limits.
decisions.compatibility_consequences: The token's declared algorithm and a compatible public issuer key must produce a valid signature.
decisions.wire_consequences: ID Tokens with unverifiable signatures, algorithm-operation disagreement, or no matching issuer key are rejected.
decisions.upstream_status: Core requires clients to validate ID Token signatures using the selected JOSE algorithm and issuer keys.
decisions.reconsider_when: A future OpenID profile changes the mandatory ID Token signature-validation mechanism.

decisions.title: The ID Token audience contains the client ID and no untrusted audience
decisions.specification: OpenID Connect Core 1.0 incorporating errata set 2
decisions.issue: Signature validity does not prove that an ID Token was issued for this client; the client must be one of the token audiences.
interpretations: Accept any signed audience; infer the audience from `azp`; or require the configured client ID in the `aud` claim and reject untrusted additional audiences.
decisions.peer_behavior: The official Core claims vector and provider-issued token bind the audience to the client identifier.
decisions.selected_behavior: The ID Token `aud` claim must contain the configured client ID, every additional audience must be trusted explicitly, and the token is rejected otherwise. Separate `azp` policy remains recorded in OIDC-DEC-006 and OIDC-DEC-018.
decisions.rationale: This preserves Core's mandatory client-audience and trusted-additional-audience checks without upgrading its separate `azp` recommendations.
decisions.security_consequences: Tokens issued only for another client or carrying an untrusted additional audience cannot authenticate at this client boundary.
decisions.resource_consequences: Audience parsing and comparison remain bounded by the configured claim limits.
decisions.compatibility_consequences: Every accepted token must identify the configured client ID and no untrusted recipient in its audience set.
decisions.wire_consequences: ID Tokens omitting the configured client ID or containing an untrusted additional audience are rejected.
decisions.upstream_status: Core Section 3.1.3.7 requires the audience to contain the client's registered client ID.
decisions.reconsider_when: A future OpenID profile replaces client ID audience binding with another mandatory recipient-binding mechanism.

decisions.title: A present authorized-party claim identifies this client
decisions.specification: OpenID Connect Core 1.0 incorporating errata set 2
decisions.issue: When an extension supplies `azp`, the client should validate the authorized party instead of ignoring a claim that can disambiguate the token recipient.
interpretations: Ignore `azp`; validate it only under an extension-specific profile; or require a present `azp` to equal the configured client ID.
decisions.peer_behavior: Provider and client libraries vary because Core makes authorized-party validation extension-aware and recommended rather than universally mandatory.
decisions.selected_behavior: When `azp` is present, it must be a non-empty string equal to the configured client ID. The package's stricter requirement for `azp` with multiple audiences remains defensive policy in OIDC-DEC-006.
decisions.rationale: This preserves Core's recommendation without upgrading the source to a universal MUST or claiming that Core requires `azp` for every multi-audience token.
decisions.security_consequences: A present authorized-party claim cannot identify a different client without rejection.
decisions.resource_consequences: The bounded claim is compared once to the configured client ID.
decisions.compatibility_consequences: Tokens with a present `azp` naming another party are rejected; absence is governed separately by the multi-audience defensive profile.
decisions.wire_consequences: A present `azp` must equal the configured client ID.
decisions.upstream_status: Core recommends extension-aware `azp` validation and says clients should verify a present value against their client ID.
decisions.reconsider_when: A supported extension profile defines a different authorized-party validation rule.

decisions.title: A sent nonce is present and matches exactly
decisions.specification: OpenID Connect Core 1.0 incorporating errata set 2
decisions.issue: When an authentication request sent a nonce, accepting an ID Token without the same nonce breaks the request-to-token binding.
interpretations: Ignore nonce; accept absence; normalize nonce values; or require presence and exact equality to the value sent in the authentication request.
decisions.peer_behavior: OIDC clients commonly expose nonce validation hooks, but callback ownership and replay storage differ.
decisions.selected_behavior: When a caller supplies a nonce validation contract for a sent nonce, the ID Token must contain the nonce and its value must match exactly. Missing or mismatched nonce is rejected.
decisions.rationale: This preserves Core's mandatory sent-nonce presence and equality check separately from the package's callback, ordering, cancellation, and replay-storage policy.
decisions.security_consequences: The ID Token remains bound to the initiating authentication request and cannot be substituted across nonce contexts.
decisions.resource_consequences: Nonce validation runs once within existing token and callback bounds.
decisions.compatibility_consequences: Callers that sent a nonce must supply a validator capable of checking its exact value.
decisions.wire_consequences: A missing or mismatched nonce claim causes rejection when nonce validation is required.
decisions.upstream_status: Core Section 3.1.3.7 requires presence and exact checking when a nonce was sent.
decisions.reconsider_when: A future OpenID profile replaces nonce request binding with another mandatory mechanism.

decisions.title: Presented front-channel token hashes match exactly
decisions.specification: OpenID Connect Core 1.0 incorporating errata set 2
decisions.issue: Front-channel access tokens and authorization codes need an exact cryptographic binding to the ID Token when their hash claims are used.
interpretations: Trust presence of the hash claim; compare an implementation-defined encoding; or compute the algorithm-defined left-half hash and require exact equality.
decisions.peer_behavior: OIDC libraries vary in whether flow context and front-channel values are supplied to low-level ID Token validators.
decisions.selected_behavior: When `ValidateIDToken` is asked to bind an access token or authorization code, the corresponding `at_hash` or `c_hash` claim must be present and must exactly match the algorithm-defined left-half hash. The API does not infer flow context when no value is supplied.
decisions.rationale: Core requires the claim value to match the computed hash; the package's explicit-input API supplies the otherwise unavailable flow context without claiming the hash is mandatory in every flow.
decisions.security_consequences: Exact hash binding prevents access-token or authorization-code substitution in the validated front-channel response.
decisions.resource_consequences: Hash work is bounded by the caller-supplied token/code and supported signing algorithm.
decisions.compatibility_consequences: A requested binding fails when the corresponding claim is absent, malformed, unsupported, or mismatched.
decisions.wire_consequences: Presented `at_hash` and `c_hash` claims must match their corresponding values exactly when validation is requested.
decisions.upstream_status: Core Sections 3.2.2.9 and 3.3.2.10 require present front-channel hash claims to match the algorithm-defined value.
decisions.reconsider_when: A future OpenID profile replaces these hash bindings or defines additional supported signing-algorithm hash families.

decisions.title: Discovery advertises the mandatory RS256 baseline
decisions.specification: OpenID Connect Discovery 1.0 incorporating errata set 2
decisions.issue: Discovery requires `id_token_signing_alg_values_supported` to include RS256 as the interoperable signing baseline.
interpretations: Accept any non-empty algorithm list; accept only caller-configured algorithms; or require RS256 in addition to every configured algorithm.
decisions.peer_behavior: The pinned Google metadata and Keycloak provider advertise RS256.
decisions.selected_behavior: Provider metadata must advertise RS256 in `id_token_signing_alg_values_supported`.
decisions.rationale: The RS256 requirement comes directly from Discovery; requiring other configured algorithms remains the package's separate capability-consistency policy.
decisions.security_consequences: The client does not silently accept a provider profile that omits OpenID Connect's mandatory signing baseline.
decisions.resource_consequences: Algorithm-list validation is bounded by the metadata limits.
decisions.compatibility_consequences: Providers omitting RS256 are rejected even when another locally supported algorithm overlaps.
decisions.wire_consequences: Discovery metadata without RS256 in the advertised ID Token signing algorithm list is invalid.
decisions.upstream_status: Discovery Section 3 requires RS256 in the advertised ID Token signing algorithm list.
decisions.reconsider_when: A later Discovery version replaces RS256 as the mandatory algorithm baseline.
